meta.label: Mission-driven businesses
meta.attribution: Reviewed 2026-06; curated from public certifications, ownership structures, impact reports, financial/SEC disclosures, and company transparency pages - not audited data and not an endorsement. Mission claims can change after acquisitions or pivots; check current ownership before relying on a brand story. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare mission-driven businesses by certification, cost, ownership, and disclosure.

axes.label: Cost or overall fit
axes.question: Lower cost or a stronger overall fit?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Patagonia

certification.note: Patagonia remains listed as a Certified B Corporation and publishes footprint/social responsibility material.

ownership.note: Patagonia says Holdfast Collective owns 98% nonvoting stock and Patagonia Purpose Trust owns 2% voting stock to protect purpose.

transparency.note: Patagonia publishes environmental and social footprint reporting, including supply-chain and product-impact material.

environment.note: Patagonia says excess profits after reinvestment are distributed to Holdfast Collective for climate, nature and community work.

longevity.note: Patagonia describes itself as 50-plus years into its responsible-business experiment.

economical.note: Patagonia sells premium outdoor apparel and gear, so values leadership comes with a high upfront price.

products.description: Outdoor apparel and gear company, now steward-owned via a purpose trust that directs profit to environmental causes.

products.name: Equal Exchange

certification.note: Equal Exchange was founded around fair trade and long-term small-farmer trading relationships.

ownership.note: Equal Exchange describes itself as worker-owned: worker members share profits/losses and vote on major decisions.

transparency.note: The cooperative explains its model and history publicly, though it is not a listed public company.

environment.note: Equal Exchange emphasizes organic/small-farmer supply chains rather than scale-maximizing commodity sourcing.

longevity.note: Equal Exchange traces its founding to 1986.

economical.note: Equal Exchange food and coffee are generally mid-priced fair-trade goods, not the cheapest commodity option.

products.description: A worker-owned cooperative that pioneered fair trade in coffee, chocolate, and food, governed one-member-one-vote.

products.name: Dr. Bronner's

certification.note: Dr. Bronner's reports regenerative organic/fair-trade sourcing work but announced it would not renew B Corp certification after expiration.

ownership.note: Dr. Bronner's is family-owned and describes progressive business practices including a 5-to-1 executive salary cap.

transparency.note: The annual All-One Report publishes corporate social responsibility and sustainability data.

environment.note: The All-One Report covers regenerative organic and fair-trade sourcing plus sustainability goals.

longevity.note: Dr. Bronner's traces its soapmaking company history to 1948.

economical.note: Concentrated soaps are mid-priced: more expensive than commodity soap, but diluted use can stretch value.

products.description: Family-owned maker of castile soaps, mission-bound with capped executive pay, regenerative sourcing, and an explicit break with B Corp renewal.

products.name: Ecosia

certification.note: Ecosia is listed as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Ecosia's milestone page describes the company as not-for-profit and dedicating 100% of profits to the planet.

transparency.note: Ecosia publishes monthly financial reports covering tree-planting and climate investments.

environment.note: Ecosia says it has planted more than 200 million trees and funds climate projects from search revenue.

longevity.note: Ecosia was founded in 2009.

economical.note: Ecosia is free to use as a search engine.

products.description: A steward-owned search engine that puts profit into planting trees and publishes monthly financials.

products.name: Riverford Organic

certification.note: Riverford Organic Farmers is listed as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Riverford says 100% of the company is held in an Employee Trust for the equal benefit of employees.

transparency.note: Riverford publishes its farming practices and B Corp/organic positioning, but remains a private company.

environment.note: Riverford's core model is organic veg boxes and organic farming.

longevity.note: B Lab records Riverford as founded by Guy Singh-Watson in Devon in 1987.

economical.note: Riverford boxes are mid-range/premium relative to commodity supermarket produce.

products.description: An employee-owned UK organic farm and veg-box service, owned by its staff since 2018.

products.name: Triodos Bank

certification.note: Triodos Bank says it became B Corp certified in 2015 and reported a B Corp score of 131.3.

ownership.note: Triodos depository receipts are issued through the Foundation for the Administration of Triodos Bank Shares.

transparency.note: Triodos publishes where money goes through project/loan transparency tools.

environment.note: Triodos positions itself as a sustainable bank financing positive-impact sectors.

longevity.note: Triodos traces its banking history to 1980.

economical.note: Triodos is usually mid-priced banking rather than a no-frills cheapest-account option.

products.description: An ethical bank that finances only sustainable projects and publishes every loan it makes.

products.name: The Co-operative Group

certification.note: Co-op has Fairtrade and ethical-retail commitments but is not primarily defined by a single certification.

ownership.note: Co-op is member-owned and governed through cooperative membership structures.

transparency.note: Co-op publishes social value and sustainability reporting.

environment.note: Co-op publishes sustainability commitments across community, climate and ethical trade.

longevity.note: The Co-operative Group traces its roots to the Rochdale Pioneers in 1844.

economical.note: Co-op is a mainstream UK convenience/grocery retailer with mid-range pricing.

products.description: One of the world's largest consumer co-operatives, with member-owned grocery, funeral, and legal services in the UK.

products.name: Fairphone

certification.note: Fairphone is listed as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Fairphone is a social enterprise focused on fairer electronics rather than steward/co-op ownership.

transparency.note: Fairphone impact materials report work on fair materials, good working conditions, long-lasting design, reuse and recycling.

environment.note: B Lab summarizes Fairphone's impact around long-lasting design, fair materials, working conditions, reuse and recycling.

longevity.note: Fairphone has operated since 2013, making it younger than many long-running mission businesses.

economical.note: Fairphone devices are premium upfront compared with many budget Android phones.

products.description: A social enterprise building modular, repairable phones with fairer materials and an open supply chain.

products.name: Tony's Chocolonely

certification.note: Tony's is listed as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Tony's Mission Lock uses a golden share and independent Mission Guardians to protect the mission across shareholder structures.

transparency.note: Tony's says it uses 100% traceable cocoa and publishes FAIR reports.

environment.note: Tony's Open Chain reports verified deforestation-free supply-chain work but the core mission is cocoa exploitation, not lowest-carbon chocolate.

longevity.note: Tony's traces its founding to 2005.

economical.note: Tony's chocolate is mid-range to premium relative to commodity chocolate bars.

products.description: A chocolate company on a mission to end slavery in cocoa, with a mission-locked golden share and traceable beans.

products.name: Numi Organic Tea

certification.note: Numi Organic Tea is listed as a Certified B Corporation and describes Fair Trade/organic sourcing.

ownership.note: Numi is founder-led rather than co-op/steward-owned.

transparency.note: Numi publishes impact reporting and public fair-trade/fair-labor sourcing material.

environment.note: Numi reports high organic certification coverage and packaging/climate initiatives in impact materials.

longevity.note: Numi was founded in 1999.

economical.note: Numi is mid-priced/premium tea compared with commodity supermarket tea.

products.description: An organic, fair-trade tea company, founder-led and B Corp certified, with disclosed sourcing.

products.name: King Arthur Baking Company

certification.note: King Arthur is a founding Certified B Corp and Vermont Benefit Corporation.

ownership.note: King Arthur describes employee-owners as central to its impact model; B Lab also lists the company as Certified B Corp.

transparency.note: The impact page and B Lab profile give public, third-party-facing accountability signals.

environment.note: King Arthur frames its benefit-corp commitments around bakers, employee-owners, farmers and the planet, but flour remains an agricultural product.

longevity.note: B Lab describes King Arthur as America's oldest flour company, serving bakers since 1790.

economical.note: Flour and mixes are widely available pantry staples, though King Arthur is usually premium versus store-brand flour.

products.description: A 100% employee-owned baking company and founding B Corp with unusually long roots in an everyday pantry category.

products.name: Organic Valley

certification.note: Organic Valley sells USDA Certified Organic food and says the co-op helped shape organic standards before USDA regulation.

ownership.note: Organic Valley says it is owned and run by organic farmers working cooperatively.

transparency.note: Organic Valley publishes an annual impact report with farm, climate and animal-care metrics.

environment.note: Its 2025 impact page reports lower average dairy-farm emissions than conventional farms and long-running organic agriculture benefits.

longevity.note: Organic Valley describes itself as farmer-owned since 1988.

economical.note: Organic dairy and eggs are widely retailed but typically cost more than conventional store-brand equivalents.

products.description: A farmer-owned organic dairy and food co-op that makes cooperative ownership visible in a mainstream grocery aisle.

products.name: REI Co-op

certification.note: REI is not mainly a B Corp-style certification story; its strongest structural signal is the consumer co-op model.

ownership.note: REI says it is a consumer cooperative and reports financial results to members.

transparency.note: REI publishes impact reports, annual financial results and audited financial statements.

environment.note: The 2025 impact report covers sustainable/inclusive products and public-lands advocacy, while REI remains a large gear retailer.

longevity.note: REI's official history dates the co-op to 1938.

economical.note: REI is accessible for many US shoppers but outdoor gear is often mid-priced to premium.

products.description: A large US outdoor retailer structured as a consumer co-op, with strong reporting and real limits from being a gear-selling business.

products.name: Suma Wholefoods

certification.note: Suma's certification signal is mixed: strong ethical buying, organic/fair-trade/cruelty-free sourcing, but not a simple B Corp badge.

ownership.note: Suma says it is Europe's largest equal-pay worker co-op.

transparency.note: Suma publishes ethical statements and sustainability reporting around buying, work and environmental goals.

environment.note: Workers.coop describes Suma as delivering vegetarian, vegan, organic, free-from, fairly traded and sustainable products.

longevity.note: Suma's buying statement says the worker-owned cooperative has sourced ethically since 1977.

economical.note: Wholefoods, ethical sourcing and UK wholesale access are mid-priced rather than bargain-basement.

products.description: A UK wholefoods wholesaler run as an equal-pay worker co-op, useful as a clear example of democratic workplace ownership.

products.name: Kickstarter PBC

certification.note: Kickstarter is a Public Benefit Corporation with a published charter rather than a conventional shareholder-only company.

ownership.note: Kickstarter's charter embeds public-benefit commitments, but PBC status is weaker than worker-, member- or steward-ownership.

transparency.note: Kickstarter publishes annual benefit statements; its 2025 statement reports against its public-benefit charter.

environment.note: Kickstarter's mission is creative funding, not environmental leadership; environmental value depends on the projects users back.

longevity.note: Kickstarter's about page says it became a Public Benefit Corporation to commit to its principles as much as profits.

economical.note: Browsing and backing are accessible globally, while creator fees and project risks remain part of the platform model.

products.description: A creative crowdfunding platform that converted to public-benefit-company status and reports against a mission charter.

products.name: Back Market

certification.note: B Lab lists Back Market as a Certified B Corporation focused on professionally refurbished electronics.

ownership.note: Back Market is a private venture-backed marketplace, so mission lock is weaker than co-op or steward ownership.

transparency.note: Back Market publishes B Corp status and impact data around refurbished technology, but marketplace quality varies by seller.

environment.note: B Lab describes Back Market as advancing circularity by doing more with existing tech across many countries.

longevity.note: Back Market says it was founded in Paris in 2014.

economical.note: Back Market advertises refurbished tech at up to 70% off compared with new products, though warranties and seller quality matter.

products.description: A B Corp marketplace for professionally refurbished electronics, strong on circularity but less mission-locked on ownership.

products.name: Allbirds

certification.note: Allbirds historically filed as a PBC/B Corp, but 2026 SEC proxy materials discuss removing the environmental-conservation public benefit focus.

ownership.note: Investor materials now identify Smartbird, Inc.; reporting says the footwear assets were sold and the public company pivoted away from shoes.

transparency.note: The 2026 proxy/SEC trail makes the pivot unusually transparent, but also shows the original mission protections were not durable.

environment.note: The company disclosed that its new business would be less focused on environmental conservation than the former footwear mission.

longevity.note: Allbirds was founded as a footwear brand in 2016 but the public company completed a major strategic pivot in 2026.

economical.note: Allbirds footwear was premium-priced; the public-company pivot means this is now a weak fit for mission-business comparison.

products.description: A cautionary case: once a B Corp/PBC footwear icon, the public company sold the footwear business and pivoted toward AI infrastructure in 2026.

products.name: Ben & Jerry's

certification.note: Ben & Jerry's has been a Certified B Corporation and publishes social/environmental reporting.

ownership.note: Ben & Jerry's says Unilever acquisition created an independent board to preserve and expand social mission, brand integrity and product quality.

transparency.note: Social and Environmental Assessment Reports document the mission structure and reporting, though parent-company conflict is visible.

environment.note: Ben & Jerry's reports Fairtrade and climate/social-mission commitments, but it remains an ice-cream business with dairy impacts.

longevity.note: Ben & Jerry's was founded in 1978 and has maintained an explicit social mission for decades.

economical.note: Ben & Jerry's is generally mid-priced/premium packaged ice cream.

products.description: An ice-cream brand with a protected social-mission board under Unilever/Magnum ownership, but that independence has become visibly contested.

products.name: Divine Chocolate

certification.note: Divine says it is Fairtrade and farmer co-owned, with impact reports for accountability.

ownership.note: Divine says Kuapa Kokoo cocoa farmers co-own the business and share in distributable profits.

transparency.note: Divine publishes annual impact reports and explains its farmer co-ownership model.

environment.note: Divine emphasizes Fairtrade sourcing and farmer support; environmental claims are present but secondary to producer equity.

longevity.note: Divine traces its founding to 1998.

economical.note: Divine is mid-priced Fairtrade chocolate, above commodity private-label bars.

products.description: A Fairtrade chocolate company co-owned by Kuapa Kokoo cocoa farmers, with farmer-led community programs and shared distributable profits.

products.name: Who Gives A Crap

certification.note: Who Gives A Crap is a mission-led paper-goods company; its primary signal is donation/impact reporting rather than only certification.

ownership.note: The company is private and mission-driven rather than co-op or steward-owned.

transparency.note: Who Gives A Crap publishes impact information and donation totals.

environment.note: The product model emphasizes recycled/bamboo paper and lower-plastic packaging compared with conventional tissue.

longevity.note: Who Gives A Crap was founded in 2012.

economical.note: Bulk subscription toilet paper is mid-priced relative to mainstream grocery tissue.

products.description: A B Corp making forest-friendly toilet paper that donates 50% of profits to sanitation projects.

products.name: Lush

certification.note: Lush relies on cruelty-free and ethical-buying policies rather than B Corp-style certification.

ownership.note: Lush is privately held and founder-led, which preserves some independence but is not a locked-purpose structure.

transparency.note: Lush publicly describes ethical buying and campaigning, while third-party critics still flag transparency gaps.

environment.note: Lush promotes packaging-free/naked products and ethical sourcing, but beauty-product impacts and ingredient debates remain.

longevity.note: Lush was founded in 1995.

economical.note: Lush products are premium-priced relative to mainstream cosmetics/personal-care basics.

products.description: A privately held cosmetics maker known for cruelty-free products, minimal packaging, and outspoken campaigns.

products.name: Nudie Jeans

certification.note: Nudie uses organic cotton and is associated with Fair Wear reporting; denim has been 100% certified organic cotton since 2012.

ownership.note: Nudie is privately held rather than co-op or steward-owned.

transparency.note: Nudie publishes sustainability reports and production transparency material.

environment.note: Nudie's model combines organic denim with free repairs to extend garment life.

longevity.note: Nudie Jeans was founded in Gothenburg in 2001.

economical.note: Nudie jeans are premium-priced, though free repairs improve lifetime value.

products.description: A denim brand offering free repairs for life and publishing detailed, audited supply-chain transparency.

products.name: Bombas

certification.note: Bombas is listed as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Bombas is a private mission-driven company, not co-op/steward-owned.

transparency.note: Bombas publishes its one-purchased-one-donated impact model and donation-product design choices.

environment.note: Bombas' central mission is social donation rather than environmental leadership.

longevity.note: B Lab records Bombas as launched in 2013.

economical.note: Bombas socks/apparel are mid-priced/premium basics, not the cheapest commodity option.

products.description: A B Corp that donates an item to people experiencing homelessness for every product purchased.

products.name: Seventh Generation

certification.note: Seventh Generation is listed as a Certified B Corporation and describes itself as a founding B Corp.

ownership.note: Seventh Generation is owned by Unilever, which weakens mission-lock relative to independent or steward-owned models.

transparency.note: Seventh Generation highlights ingredient disclosure and publishes an ingredient glossary.

environment.note: Unilever describes Seventh Generation as focused on plant-based products and reduced environmental impact.

longevity.note: Seventh Generation says it became a founding B Corp in 2008 and has operated as a sustainability brand for decades.

economical.note: Seventh Generation is mid-priced and widely available versus niche premium green-cleaning brands.

products.description: A pioneering plant-based household-products B Corp, now owned by Unilever but retaining its certification.

products.name: Bookshop.org

certification.note: Bookshop.org is listed as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Bookshop.org says its public-benefit purpose is to give independent booksellers a direct-to-consumer ecommerce option against major retailers.

transparency.note: Its About page says it gives over 80% of its profit margin to independent bookstores and supports more than 2,500 stores.

environment.note: Bookshop.org shows climate-neutral positioning, but its core model is cultural/local-retail support rather than a low-impact physical goods supply chain.

longevity.note: Bookshop.org launched in 2020, so the mission track record is promising but still comparatively young.

economical.note: Prices are usually normal book-retail prices rather than the lowest marketplace prices, with the tradeoff that independent bookstores receive support.

products.description: A B Corp online bookstore built to route more book spending toward independent bookstores instead of dominant ecommerce platforms.

products.name: Greyston Bakery

certification.note: Greyston Bakery is listed by B Lab as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Greyston describes itself through a nonprofit social-justice enterprise and Open Hiring model rather than conventional profit-only ownership.

transparency.note: Its B Corp page explains the Open Hiring model and says B Corp status holds the bakery accountable to a third-party standard.

environment.note: The mission evidence is strongest on employment and social inclusion; environmental leadership is less central in public materials.

longevity.note: B Lab notes Greyston Bakery opened in 1982 and has long used Open Hiring to create opportunities.

economical.note: Greyston brownies and baked goods are premium specialty products rather than basic grocery staples.

products.description: A Certified B Corp bakery known for Open Hiring: using baked-goods sales to create jobs without conventional background-screen barriers.

products.name: Cabot Creamery Cooperative

certification.note: Cabot says it became a Certified B Corp in 2012 and was the world's first dairy cooperative to do so.

ownership.note: Cabot describes its B Corp work through its cooperative model and farmer-owner purpose.

transparency.note: B Lab publishes Cabot's B Impact score and category assessment, giving third-party accountability beyond brand copy.

environment.note: Cabot publishes sustainability practices such as water reuse, but dairy remains a higher-impact food category.

longevity.note: Cabot has operated since 1919, giving it one of the longer track records in the mission-business set.

economical.note: Cabot products are common in US grocery channels and often priced as mainstream premium dairy rather than niche specialty food.

products.description: A farmer-owned dairy cooperative and long-running B Corp, with strong ownership signals but the unavoidable climate tradeoffs of dairy.

products.name: Cotopaxi

certification.note: Cotopaxi says it is both a Certified B Corp and registered Public Benefit Corporation.

ownership.note: Public Benefit Corporation status adds legal mission accountability, but it is not as mission-locked as co-op or steward ownership.

transparency.note: Cotopaxi publishes impact reporting and help-center material explaining its B Corp/PBC structure.

environment.note: Cotopaxi emphasizes deadstock/repurposed fabrics and impact reporting, while still selling new outdoor apparel and gear.

longevity.note: Cotopaxi reports years of B Corp certification, but its overall company history is shorter than legacy co-ops and older mission brands.

economical.note: Outdoor packs and apparel are premium purchases, with sales and secondhand use improving but not solving affordability.

products.description: A B Corp and Public Benefit Corporation outdoor brand built around 'Gear for Good,' deadstock colorways, and poverty-alleviation giving.

products.name: Grove Collaborative

certification.note: B Lab lists Grove Collaborative as a Certified B Corp and describes it as a Public Benefit Corporation.

ownership.note: Public Benefit Corporation status gives mission accountability, but Grove is not co-op, employee-owned, or steward-owned.

transparency.note: Grove publishes sustainability reports and investor updates with plastic, carbon, forest-health, ingredient and equity metrics.

environment.note: Its 2025 sustainability release reports a 41% plastic-footprint reduction from the 2023 baseline and plastic-reducing product impacts.

longevity.note: Grove has over a decade of B Corp history, but the public-company era is newer and still evolving.

economical.note: Online household-goods subscriptions can be convenient but are usually less economical than buying commodity cleaners locally.

products.description: A B Corp and Public Benefit Corporation home-goods platform with strong plastic-reduction reporting, balanced by online subscription economics.

products.name: Newman's Own

certification.note: Newman's Own is not scored as B Corp-style certified, but its 100% profits-to-charity model is public and unusually formal.

ownership.note: AP reporting describes the company as donated to and owned through Newman's Own Foundation, with profits donated to charity under a foundation-owned enterprise model.

transparency.note: The foundation publishes its giving purpose, grantee work and portfolio approach for children facing adversity.

environment.note: The public mission is philanthropic rather than environmental; food products still carry ordinary packaged-food supply-chain impacts.

longevity.note: Newman's Own was founded in 1982 and has maintained the profits-to-charity model across decades.

economical.note: Products such as dressings, sauces and snacks are sold in mainstream grocery channels at ordinary premium-brand prices.

products.description: A grocery brand whose unusual model donates 100% of profits to charity, with strong mission ownership but less environmental specificity.

products.name: Eileen Fisher

certification.note: B Lab lists Eileen Fisher as a Certified B Corporation with a 109.4 overall B Impact score.

ownership.note: B Lab describes the company as B Corp certified and accountable to stakeholder standards, but not co-op or steward-owned.

transparency.note: Eileen Fisher publicly discusses its B Corp recertification and the hard lessons from workforce and racial-justice work.

environment.note: Eileen Fisher Renew says it has taken back more than 2 million pieces since 2009 to resell, donate or remake.

longevity.note: The company was founded in 1984 and has a decades-long responsible-fashion track record.

economical.note: Eileen Fisher apparel is premium-priced; Renew resale improves access but does not make it a low-cost clothing default.

products.description: A long-running women's apparel B Corp known for circular design and the Renew take-back/resale program.

products.name: MUD Jeans

certification.note: B Lab lists MUD Jeans International as a Certified B Corporation with an 83.8 overall B Impact score.

ownership.note: Certified mission-led apparel company, but no co-op or steward-ownership lock is evident from public materials.

transparency.note: MUD Jeans publishes sustainability reporting and lifecycle-analysis figures for water and CO2e savings.

environment.note: MUD reports large water and CO2e savings from recycled cotton, recycled water and energy-saving production techniques.

longevity.note: MUD Jeans has a focused circular-denim track record since 2012, shorter than older mission brands.

economical.note: Premium denim pricing and leasing/resale models improve circularity more than low-cost access.

products.description: A Dutch B Corp denim brand built around recycled cotton, repair, take-back, and circular jeans models.

products.name: Ethique

certification.note: Ethique publishes its B Corp status and explains B Corp's social/environmental accountability standard.

ownership.note: Mission-led private personal-care company; no co-op, steward-owned or foundation-owned lock found in public materials.

transparency.note: Ethique publishes impact reporting with wins, challenges and goals.

environment.note: Ethique reports plastic-free solid formats, 2% of sales donated and over 6,500 tonnes CO2e saved/reduced.

longevity.note: B Corp Australia describes Ethique as started in 2012 in Christchurch.

economical.note: Solid bars can last longer than liquid products, but unit prices are still above commodity shampoo/soap.

products.description: A plastic-free solid beauty and personal-care brand with B Corp accountability and unusually clear impact reporting.

products.name: MiiR

certification.note: B Lab lists MiiR as a Certified B Corporation with a 95.5 overall B Impact score.

ownership.note: Mission-led private company with a dedicated MiiR Foundation, but not co-op or steward-owned.

transparency.note: MiiR's 2025 Impact Report reports giving, responsibility and lower-impact design work.

environment.note: MiiR reports responsibility work around lower-impact materials and carbon footprint, while still selling new physical goods.

longevity.note: The 2025 report frames MiiR as marking 15 years of purpose-driven progress.

economical.note: Durable bottles and drinkware are premium purchases compared with commodity bottles/cups.

products.description: A B Corp drinkware company pairing durable products with transparent giving and a dedicated foundation.

products.name: Preserve

certification.note: B Lab lists Preserve as a Certified B Corporation focused on lower-carbon, lower-waste consumer products.

ownership.note: Certified mission-led private company; public evidence emphasizes B Corp accountability rather than co-op/steward ownership.

transparency.note: Preserve explains its B Corp certification and recycling program mechanics publicly.

environment.note: Preserve's Gimme 5 program collected #5 plastic for reuse in toothbrushes, razors and other products, with current food-service/corporate focus.

longevity.note: Preserve founded Gimme 5 in 2008 and has a long track record in recycled-plastic consumer goods.

economical.note: Toothbrushes, razors and kitchen goods are often priced near accessible green-product tiers rather than luxury tiers.

products.description: A B Corp making toothbrushes, razors, tableware and housewares from recycled #5 plastic, with a long recycling-program history.

products.name: Better World Books

certification.note: B Lab lists Better World Books as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Better World Books is mission-aligned around libraries/literacy, but not structured as a consumer co-op or steward-owned firm.

transparency.note: B Lab reports lifetime figures for books donated, literacy/library funding and books reused or recycled.

environment.note: B Lab reports Better World Books has reused or recycled more than 475 million books.

longevity.note: B Lab says the company launched in 2003, giving it a two-decade social-enterprise track record.

economical.note: Used-book resale can be affordable while also funding literacy and library partners.

products.description: A used-book B Corp that routes resale into literacy funding, donated books, and book reuse/recycling.

products.name: Too Good To Go

certification.note: B Lab lists Too Good To Go as a Certified B Corporation with a 93.4 B Impact Score.

ownership.note: Too Good To Go is a private mission company rather than a co-op or steward-owned firm, but its public mission is explicitly food-waste reduction.

transparency.note: Too Good To Go publishes ESG and impact reporting, including B Corp recertification details and impact-report materials.

environment.note: B Lab reports that Too Good To Go has helped save more than 300 million meals from going to waste, avoiding substantial CO2e, water and land use.

longevity.note: The company launched in 2016 and has expanded internationally, giving it a meaningful but still young track record.

economical.note: The model sells surplus food at reduced prices, so users can save money while reducing waste.

products.description: A B Corp marketplace for buying surplus meals from restaurants and grocers before they become food waste.

products.name: Olio

certification.note: B Lab lists Olio Exchange Limited as a Certified B Corporation with a 94.0 B Impact Score.

ownership.note: Olio is a community-sharing platform rather than a co-op, with a mission centered on local sharing and waste prevention.

transparency.note: Olio publishes impact information and links its B Corp impact report from its impact page.

environment.note: Olio's impact model tracks food saved, exchanges completed and waste avoided across food and non-food sharing.

longevity.note: Olio has moved beyond food sharing into wider local reuse, suggesting a broader durability of the sharing model.

economical.note: The user value proposition is free local sharing of food and household items, making it highly accessible when there is local activity.

products.description: A B Corp local-sharing app for giving away food and household items so useful things stay in use.

products.name: Fairbnb.coop

certification.note: Fairbnb.coop is not presented as a B Corp in reviewed sources; the certification score reflects its cooperative/legal model rather than B Lab certification.

ownership.note: Fairbnb.coop describes itself as a cooperative platform putting people over profit and reinvesting in communities.

transparency.note: The platform states that 50% of booking fees are donated to community projects in the destination.

environment.note: Fairbnb.coop is a more community-centered tourism platform, but travel stays still carry tourism and transport impacts.

longevity.note: The service launched publicly in 2019, so it has a shorter track record than older co-ops and social enterprises.

economical.note: Short-stay travel is not inherently low-cost, and community-fee funding can make it less price-driven than extractive marketplaces.

products.description: A cooperative short-stay platform that routes half its booking fee into local community projects.

environment.note: B Lab describes Wildling as sourcing regenerative, natural materials such as hemp, linen, cotton and wool.

longevity.note: Wildling's B Corp record is newer than long-running legacy mission companies, so track-record scoring is moderate.

economical.note: Wildling shoes are specialized minimalist footwear and generally cost more than mainstream casual shoes.

products.description: A B Corp minimalist-shoe brand using natural and regenerative material claims, strongest for footwear values rather than affordability.

products.name: Room & Board

certification.note: Room & Board says it became a Certified B Corporation in 2023, and B Lab lists the company in its directory.

ownership.note: B Lab describes Room & Board as a 100% employee-owned furniture and home-decor retailer.

transparency.note: Room & Board publishes sustainability pages and impact reporting on materials, craft, donations and B Corp certification.

environment.note: Room & Board says sustainable practices have been fundamental since 1980 and that it uses 100% sustainably sourced wood in products.

longevity.note: B Lab says Room & Board was founded in 1980 and has built a long-running furniture-retail reputation.

economical.note: Room & Board sells durable modern furniture, but prices are premium compared with secondhand, flat-pack or mass-market furniture.

products.description: A rare large employee-owned B Corp furniture retailer, strong on ownership and longevity but mostly relevant for higher-budget durable purchases.

products.name: Signal Foundation / Signal Messenger

certification.note: Signal is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit rather than a B Corp or product-certification model, so the certification score reflects legal nonprofit status.

ownership.note: Signal says it is an independent nonprofit with no ads, no affiliate marketers, no creepy tracking, and no major-tech acquisition path.

transparency.note: Signal Foundation describes a 501(c)(3) Foundation plus LLC structure, board, open-source mission and donation-supported model.

environment.note: Signal's public mission evidence is strongest on privacy and governance; it does not publish a broad environmental impact program on the cited pages.

longevity.note: Signal says Signal Messenger originated in 2012 and the Foundation formed in 2018 to support its growth and operations.

economical.note: Signal says its app is free for everyone and supported by grants and donations from users.

products.description: A nonprofit messaging service with unusually strong mission lock for privacy and no-ad communication; environmental evidence is limited, but the governance model is a standout.

products.name: Mozilla / Firefox

certification.note: Mozilla is not scored as a B Corp; its checkable mission evidence comes from nonprofit public records, manifesto commitments and open-source work.

ownership.note: Mozilla publicly ties its family of products and organizations to the Mozilla Manifesto and a not-for-profit Mozilla Foundation.

transparency.note: Mozilla Foundation publishes annual reports, Form 990s, audited financial statements, bylaws and subsidiary public records.

environment.note: Mozilla's strongest public commitments are around open internet, privacy and public benefit; the cited mission documents are not primarily environmental.

longevity.note: Mozilla says the project has worked since 1998 and is best known for creating the Firefox browser.

economical.note: Firefox and many Mozilla public-interest tools are free to use, though Mozilla now includes a broader portfolio of paid and advertising-adjacent products.

products.description: A long-running open-web institution with strong transparency and public-interest roots, balanced by the reality that Mozilla now runs a mixed nonprofit, product and advertising-adjacent portfolio.

products.name: Mastodon

certification.note: Mastodon is free/open-source and mission-led, but not scored as a B Corp or consumer-product certification route.

ownership.note: Mastodon says the software is developed by a non-profit organization and that public support sustains development.

transparency.note: The project links source code, documentation, roadmap, support and donation paths, making the technical route unusually inspectable.

environment.note: Mastodon's public mission evidence is about decentralization, ads, user control and open protocols, not a documented environmental program.

longevity.note: Mastodon has operated as a recognizable fediverse platform since the mid-2010s and continues to publish current software, docs and donation channels.

economical.note: The core software is free and open source, though individual servers may ask for donations or subscriptions to cover hosting and moderation.

products.description: A decentralized, open-source social platform with no central ad feed and strong user-control signals; quality and moderation still depend heavily on the server you choose.

products.name: Bob's Red Mill

certification.note: Bob's Red Mill emphasizes employee ownership, Non-GMO Project verification and zero-waste certification rather than company-wide B Corp status.

ownership.note: Bob's Red Mill says it became 100% employee-owned in 2020 after starting an ESOP in 2010.

transparency.note: The company publishes employee-ownership details, sustainability pages, an impact report link, quality information and supply-chain disclosure links.

environment.note: Bob's Red Mill says it earned TRUE Gold zero-waste certification by diverting 92% of waste from landfill and saved 2,913 tons of food waste in 2025.

longevity.note: Bob's Red Mill says Bob and Charlee Moore founded the company in 1978, giving it a long operating history before and after ESOP transition.

economical.note: The brand sells widely distributed staple grains, flours and baking products, making it more accessible than many premium mission brands.

products.description: A familiar pantry brand with a rare 100% employee-owned structure and credible zero-waste/sustainability signals, strongest where you already buy grains or baking staples.

products.name: Tillamook County Creamery Association

certification.note: Tillamook's stewardship page states that Tillamook County Creamery Association is a Certified B Corp.

ownership.note: Tillamook describes itself as accountable to farmer-owners and frames stewardship through its cooperative model.

transparency.note: Tillamook publishes stewardship commitments and directs readers to past stewardship reports for progress tracking.

environment.note: Tillamook names enduring ecosystems among its stewardship commitments, including conserving air, land and water while reducing energy and waste.

longevity.note: The association's farmer-owned co-op identity and stewardship reporting sit on a long-running regional dairy brand rather than a recent campaign.

economical.note: Tillamook products are mainstream grocery items, though dairy and premium branded foods are not the lowest-cost or lowest-impact default.

products.description: A farmer-owned dairy cooperative and Certified B Corp with unusually visible stewardship reporting for a mainstream grocery brand; still a dairy choice, not a low-impact food shortcut.

products.name: Ocean Spray

certification.note: Ocean Spray's strongest mission evidence is cooperative ownership and sustainability reporting rather than B Corp or broad product certification.

ownership.note: Ocean Spray describes itself as a farmer-owned agricultural cooperative and globally recognized brand.

transparency.note: Ocean Spray publishes a purpose page, cooperative values and a Cooperative Sustainability Report and Strategy organized around Planet, Product, People and Prosperity.

environment.note: The cooperative says its sustainability report and strategy are meant to keep it aligned as a regenerative and resilient cooperative for generations.

longevity.note: Ocean Spray's cooperative structure and mainstream brand recognition make it a long-running example of farmer-owner control at consumer scale.

economical.note: Ocean Spray products are widely distributed grocery items, generally more accessible than niche mission-brand alternatives.

products.description: A mainstream farmer-owned cranberry cooperative, useful as a recognizable co-op example; certification depth is thinner than B Corp peers, and many products still need ordinary nutrition judgment.

products.name: Ritual

certification.note: B Lab lists Ritual as a Certified B Corporation with a 104.2 overall B Impact Score and certification since May 2022.

ownership.note: Ritual has B Corp mission-lock evidence, but the cited sources do not show worker, co-op, nonprofit or steward ownership.

transparency.note: B Lab says Ritual publicly shares suppliers and manufacturing locations, and Ritual frames its own standard as Made Traceable.

environment.note: Ritual says it publicly shares product carbon footprints and uses LCA-based accounting to find reduction opportunities.

longevity.note: Ritual's current B Corp certification and traceability work are strong, but the company is younger than the long-running co-op and employee-owned examples.

economical.note: Ritual sells premium subscription supplements; mission evidence is strong, but affordability is weaker than ordinary grocery or generic supplement routes.

products.description: A B Corp supplement brand with unusually strong ingredient and carbon-footprint transparency, but a premium subscription model and no claim here that supplements are medically necessary.

products.name: John Lewis Partnership

certification.note: John Lewis Partnership is not scored here as a B Corp; the verified mission signal is its long-running employee-owned partnership structure.

ownership.note: The company describes itself as the UK's largest employee-owned business, where employees are called Partners.

transparency.note: John Lewis Partnership publishes annual reports and accounts, plus separate ethics and sustainability reporting.

environment.note: Its ethics and sustainability reporting discloses progress and challenges, but the business remains a large retail and grocery operation.

longevity.note: The partnership traces its employee-ownership model to founder John Spedan Lewis and a long-running experiment in industrial democracy.

economical.note: John Lewis and Waitrose are mainstream UK retailers, but not the lowest-cost default compared with discount retailers.

products.description: A large UK retail partnership where employee ownership is the core values signal; strong on governance, less simple as a low-impact consumption route.

products.name: MONDRAGON Corporation

certification.note: MONDRAGON is not a product certification; its mission signal is the formal cooperative business project and democratic organization values it publishes.

ownership.note: MONDRAGON describes itself as a cooperative business project built around intercooperation, grassroots management and democratic organization.

transparency.note: Its annual-report material discloses group sales, employment, profits and business-area performance.

environment.note: MONDRAGON includes corporate social responsibility among its values, but it is a diversified industrial, finance, retail and knowledge group rather than a single low-impact product business.

longevity.note: MONDRAGON says the cooperative business project was launched in 1956 and now spans multiple business areas.

economical.note: As a federation and business group, MONDRAGON is less a single consumer-price choice than an ownership-model benchmark.

products.description: A global reference point for worker-cooperative business at scale; excellent for ownership-model literacy, less directly comparable to a single consumer brand.

products.name: EarthHero

certification.note: EarthHero says it is a Certified B Corporation and also references 1% for the Planet and Climate Neutral partnerships.

ownership.note: EarthHero's reviewed public material shows a mission-led marketplace, not co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: EarthHero publishes impact criteria and explains its marketplace screening and 1% for the Planet giving.

environment.note: EarthHero centers product screening, environmental giving and sustainability initiatives across its marketplace.

longevity.note: The company has current mission certifications and impact pages, but a shorter operating record than long-running co-ops or legacy mission brands.

economical.note: EarthHero sells curated sustainable products, which often cost more than commodity marketplace equivalents.

products.description: A curated sustainable-products marketplace, useful when shoppers want one place to compare lower-waste goods, but still a consumption marketplace.

products.name: Coyuchi

certification.note: Coyuchi's impact material emphasizes certified organic cotton and other textile standards across bedding, bath and home goods.

ownership.note: Coyuchi is scored as a mission-led private brand; the reviewed sources do not show co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: Coyuchi publishes impact reports and impact pages describing materials, circularity and product standards.

environment.note: Coyuchi centers organic cotton, circular programs and lower-impact home textiles, while home textiles remain material-intensive goods.

longevity.note: Coyuchi has an established organic-home-textiles track record and publishes multi-year impact material.

economical.note: Coyuchi's organic bedding and home textiles are premium-priced compared with mainstream home-goods retailers.

products.description: A premium organic bedding and home-textile brand with strong material standards and impact reporting, but weak affordability.

products.name: Naturepedic

certification.note: Naturepedic publishes a certifications page for organic, emissions and product-safety standards including GOTS and GREENGUARD Gold.

ownership.note: Naturepedic's mission is founder-led organic sleep rather than co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance in the reviewed sources.

transparency.note: The company publishes product certification detail and an origin story explaining its chemical-avoidance mission.

environment.note: Naturepedic focuses on certified organic materials and avoiding conventional mattress materials such as polyurethane foam, flame retardants and fiberglass.

longevity.note: Naturepedic says it was born in 2003 and has continued its organic mattress and bedding focus since then.

economical.note: Certified organic mattresses are premium purchases, making the values signal strong but affordability weak.

products.description: A certified organic mattress and bedding company with strong material-safety credentials, best treated as a premium health/environment choice.

products.name: World Centric

certification.note: World Centric says its 2025 B Corp recertification yielded a 126.2 score, and it publishes compostability-certification material.

ownership.note: World Centric's mission page says it gives 25% of profits to grassroots social and environmental organizations, but it is not scored as co-op or steward-owned.

transparency.note: World Centric publishes B Corp, sustainability and compostability-certification information for its foodservice products.

environment.note: The company makes compostable and reusable foodservice products and frames them around renewable plant-based materials and commercial composting.

longevity.note: World Centric says it has been a Certified B Corp since 2013, with a 2025 recertification.

economical.note: Certified compostable foodservice ware is usually pricier than conventional disposable packaging and depends on composting infrastructure.

products.description: A compostable foodservice-products company with unusually strong donation and certification signals, but dependent on real commercial composting access.

products.name: Stonyfield Organic

certification.note: B Lab lists Lactalis US Yogurt, d/b/a Stonyfield Farm, as a Certified B Corporation with a 97.3 overall B Impact Score.

ownership.note: Stonyfield's B Corp profile is under Lactalis US Yogurt, so the mission brand sits inside a large dairy corporation rather than independent or co-op ownership.

transparency.note: Stonyfield publishes annual impact reporting on farms, emissions, energy efficiency, packaging and community work.

environment.note: Its impact report focuses on direct-supply organic farms, greenhouse-gas reductions and organic agriculture benefits, while dairy still has material climate impacts.

longevity.note: Stonyfield says it has advocated for organic farming and the planet since its origins in 1983.

economical.note: Organic yogurt is more accessible than many premium mission products, but it remains pricier than commodity dairy or not buying dairy.

products.description: A long-running organic dairy brand with B Corp and impact-reporting signals, but weaker mission lock because it is owned by a large dairy corporation.

products.name: Eco-Products

certification.note: B Lab lists Eco-Products, PBC as a Certified B Corporation, and Eco-Products says it has been certified since 2016.

ownership.note: Eco-Products is a Public Benefit Corporation, which gives more mission structure than ordinary corporate governance but is weaker than co-op or steward ownership.

transparency.note: Eco-Products publishes B Corp certification information and impact-report material about compostable packaging and waste diversion.

environment.note: Eco-Products focuses on compostable foodservice packaging, waste diversion and products made with renewable or recycled materials.

longevity.note: Eco-Products reports B Corp certification since 2016 and multiple recertification cycles.

economical.note: Compostable packaging usually costs more than conventional disposable packaging and only works well where composting systems accept it.

products.description: A Public Benefit Corporation foodservice-packaging brand with B Corp certification; useful for institutional purchasing, but not a substitute for reuse.

products.name: ECOS

certification.note: ECOS publishes sustainability qualifications including carbon-neutral, water-neutral, TRUE Platinum Zero Waste, vegan and cruelty-free claims.

ownership.note: ECOS says it has been family-owned and operated since 1967, and its sustainability report describes it as women-owned, minority-owned and family-owned.

transparency.note: ECOS publishes sustainability reports and impact pages on manufacturing, carbon, water, waste and product commitments.

environment.note: ECOS says its U.S. facilities are climate positive and highlights renewable energy, water restoration and zero-waste manufacturing work.

longevity.note: ECOS says it has been family-owned and operated since 1967.

economical.note: ECOS explicitly frames safer cleaning as affordable and is widely sold compared with many refill-only niche brands.

products.description: A long-running family-owned cleaning-products company with strong manufacturing sustainability claims and better accessibility than many niche green brands.

products.name: Minor Figures

certification.note: B Lab lists Minor Figures as a Certified B Corporation with an 89.9 overall B Impact Score.

ownership.note: Minor Figures has B Corp accountability, but the cited sources do not show co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: Minor Figures publishes B Corp impact reports discussing certification, product changes and sustainability work.

environment.note: Its 2024 B Corp impact report describes product changes intended to reduce packaging weight, shipping space and emissions from Barista Oat.

longevity.note: Minor Figures' B Lab profile shows certification progress since 2022, but the company is younger than legacy mission brands.

economical.note: Minor Figures oat drinks are a premium plant-based beverage option rather than the cheapest milk alternative.

products.description: A B Corp oat-drink brand with current impact reporting, strongest as a plant-based coffee option rather than a low-cost staple.

products.name: Beneficial State Bank

certification.note: B Lab lists Beneficial State Bank as a Certified B Corporation, and the bank describes itself as a certified B Corp bank and CDFI.

ownership.note: Beneficial State says its equity capital is majority-owned by the nonprofit Beneficial State Foundation, creating a stronger mission lock than ordinary shareholder ownership.

transparency.note: The bank publishes impact reporting and describes its lending, community and environmental priorities publicly.

environment.note: Beneficial State frames banking as an impact lever and positions its lending and deposits around communities and do-no-harm enterprises.

longevity.note: Beneficial State Bank has a mature regional banking record, but is younger than legacy co-ops and century-old mission retailers.

economical.note: Its regional banking model offers ordinary banking products, but availability is narrower than national megabanks and credit unions.

products.description: A B Corp and CDFI bank with nonprofit-majority ownership, useful as a mission-lock example for moving deposits toward community finance.

products.name: Amalgamated Bank

certification.note: Amalgamated says it has been a Certified B Corporation since 2017, and B Lab lists the bank as certified.

ownership.note: The bank has B Corp governance accountability, but the cited sources do not show co-op, nonprofit-owned or steward-owned control.

transparency.note: Amalgamated publishes public pages on B Corp responsibility and values-aligned banking, including fossil-fuel-free investment options.

environment.note: The bank offers a fossil-fuel-free investing portfolio and frames dollars as a tool for cleaner-world outcomes.

longevity.note: Amalgamated has a long operating history compared with newer mission-finance entrants.

economical.note: Its account and banking products are mainstream-accessible, though mission banking may not be the lowest-fee option for every household.

products.description: A long-running socially responsible US bank with B Corp certification and fossil-fuel-free investing options, but without co-op-style ownership lock.

products.name: Cooperative Home Care Associates

certification.note: CHCA describes itself as a worker-owned, women-led and B Corp certified company.

ownership.note: PHI says CHCA employs more than 2,000 staff and is the largest worker-owned cooperative in the United States.

transparency.note: Public profiles explain CHCA's cooperative model, quality-jobs mission and home-care role, though it publishes less impact data than some B Corps.

environment.note: CHCA's mission is care work and worker ownership rather than a specifically environmental product or service.

longevity.note: CHCA was founded in 1985 and has grown from 12 home health aides into a large worker-owned agency.

economical.note: Home care pricing and eligibility depend on local payer arrangements, so this is not a simple low-cost consumer product.

products.description: A worker-owned home-care cooperative where the mission is quality care through quality jobs, not a consumer-goods halo.

products.name: Namaste Solar

certification.note: B Lab lists Namaste Solar as a Certified B Corporation, and the company publicly identifies as B Corp certified.

ownership.note: Namaste Solar says it became an employee-owned cooperative on January 1, 2011.

transparency.note: The company publishes pages explaining employee ownership, public-benefit status and its stakeholder-balancing culture.

environment.note: Namaste designs, installs and maintains solar electric systems, so the core service directly supports clean-energy adoption.

longevity.note: The company has combined employee ownership with solar installation for more than a decade.

economical.note: Solar installation can lower lifetime energy costs for some customers, but the upfront purchase is still expensive and location-specific.

products.description: A Colorado solar installer with B Corp certification and employee-owned cooperative governance, strong when clean energy and ownership both matter.

products.name: Amicus Solar Cooperative

certification.note: B Lab lists Amicus Solar Cooperative as a Certified B Corporation.

ownership.note: Amicus says it is a 100% member-owned cooperative where each company is an equal co-owner and decisions are democratic.

transparency.note: The cooperative publishes member counts, standards and purpose/values information about its values-led solar network.

environment.note: Amicus was founded to support independent solar businesses working to create a market solution to climate change.

longevity.note: B Lab reports Amicus was founded in 2011, giving it a solid but not legacy-length operating record.

economical.note: As a purchasing and standards cooperative, Amicus can strengthen local installers, but it is not a direct low-cost consumer product.

products.description: A member-owned cooperative of independent solar companies, useful as a business-structure example for clean-energy deployment.

products.name: Green Mountain Power

certification.note: Green Mountain Power says it is the first utility in the world to earn B Corp certification, and B Lab lists it as certified.

ownership.note: B Lab describes Green Mountain Power as an investor-owned electric generation and distribution utility, so ownership is not mission-locked like a co-op.

transparency.note: Its public utility pages and B Corp profile disclose certification, standards and customer/community positioning.

environment.note: GMP says it serves Vermont customers with 100% carbon-free electricity on an annual basis and works on resilience and cost-cutting programs.

longevity.note: As a regulated utility with repeated B Corp recertification, GMP has a longer track record than many startup mission brands.

economical.note: Utility costs are regulated and location-bound; GMP emphasizes affordability, but it is only available to Vermont service-area customers.

products.description: A Vermont utility with B Corp certification and carbon-free electricity claims; strong as a utility-transition example, weaker on ownership lock.

products.name: Good On You

certification.note: Good On You is scored here for its published ratings methodology, not for a B Corp or co-op certification found in the reviewed sources.

ownership.note: The useful public signal is the ratings system; the reviewed public pages do not show co-op, nonprofit-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: Good On You says its methodology evaluates up to 1,000 data points across more than 100 issues and weights third-party sources by assurance quality.

environment.note: The platform helps consumers check fashion and beauty brand impacts on people, planet and animals, though it is not itself a product manufacturer.

longevity.note: Good On You has been publicly operating as a sustainability-rating platform for years, but it is newer than legacy mission retailers.

economical.note: Its consumer brand-rating app and directory are free to use, making it highly accessible as a decision-support tool.

products.description: A free ratings platform for checking fashion and beauty brands against people, planet and animal-impact signals before buying.

products.name: Ten Thousand Villages

certification.note: Ten Thousand Villages says it is verified by the World Fair Trade Organization, and Fair Trade Federation lists it as a member.

ownership.note: Fair Trade Federation describes Ten Thousand Villages as a nonprofit fair trade retailer connecting skilled makers to the market.

transparency.note: The retailer publishes impact, fair-trade and history pages, while also acknowledging a current period of transformation and renewal.

environment.note: Its impact page names sustainable practices, including upcycled and local materials, but the catalog is still a goods retailer.

longevity.note: Ten Thousand Villages traces its history to Edna Ruth Byler's 1946 work and foregrounds that long fair-trade record.

economical.note: Many goods are accessible gifts and home items, but fair-trade handmade products are not designed to undercut commodity retail prices.

products.description: A nonprofit fair-trade retailer with an unusually long record, useful when artisan income and fair-trade structure matter more than cheapest price.

products.name: Bee's Wrap

certification.note: Bee's Wrap says it became a Certified B Corporation in 2019, and B Lab lists the company as certified.

ownership.note: The reviewed public sources show B Corp accountability, but not co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: Its B Corp and product pages explain the certification, product use limits and plastic-free food-storage role.

environment.note: Bee's Wrap replaces disposable plastic wrap with reusable beeswax-coated cotton wraps for many food-storage tasks.

longevity.note: The brand has B Corp history since 2019, but less multi-decade proof than older mission retailers.

economical.note: Reusable wraps can avoid disposable plastic purchases, but the upfront price is higher and they are not suitable for every storage task.

products.description: A B Corp reusable food-wrap brand that can replace some disposable plastic wrap, with a practical floor around cost and use limits.

products.name: Dopper

certification.note: B Lab lists Dopper B.V. as a Certified B Corporation with a high overall B Impact Score.

ownership.note: Dopper's public certification and mission materials do not show co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned control.

transparency.note: Dopper publishes impact research on reusable-bottle displacement of single-use plastic bottles.

environment.note: The company says each Dopper bottle saves the equivalent of 104 single-use plastic bottles per year, based on its impact research.

longevity.note: Dopper has a current B Corp profile and sustainability reporting, but not the long record of older mission retailers or co-ops.

economical.note: A reusable bottle can save money over bottled water, but branded bottles cost more upfront than basic refillable options.

products.description: A high-scoring B Corp reusable-bottle brand focused on reducing bottled-water waste, best read as a reuse nudge rather than a cheapest-bottle pick.

products.name: LifeStraw

certification.note: B Lab lists LifeStraw as a Certified B Corporation and notes B Corp and Climate Neutral certification claims.

ownership.note: LifeStraw's public mission and certification sources do not show co-op, nonprofit-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: LifeStraw publishes Give Back program metrics, including children and schools reached through purifier distribution.

environment.note: The B Lab profile says LifeStraw measures and minimizes product and packaging impact while supporting emergency-response work.

longevity.note: LifeStraw says it has partnered in Guinea worm eradication work for 25 years and responds to emergencies globally.

economical.note: LifeStraw filters can be practical emergency and travel tools, but they cost more than ordinary bottles and are not a universal water-access solution.

products.description: A B Corp water-filter company with a public Give Back program; useful for emergency/travel filtration and safe-water impact, not a structural fix alone.

products.name: Nimble

certification.note: B Lab lists Nimble as a Certified B Corporation, and Nimble says it became a B Corp and committed to 1% for the Planet.

ownership.note: Nimble's reviewed public materials show B Corp accountability, not co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: Nimble publishes its B Corp rationale and B Lab profile, but offers less deep public impact reporting than some larger mission brands.

environment.note: B Lab says Nimble uses more sustainable materials, 100% plastic-free packaging and free old-tech recycling.

longevity.note: Nimble is a newer mission-tech accessory brand than established electronics and repair companies.

economical.note: Nimble chargers and accessories are premium alternatives to commodity tech accessories, so affordability is a mixed signal.

products.description: A B Corp tech-accessory brand using recycled materials, plastic-free packaging and e-waste takeback, with the usual caveat that accessories are still extra consumption.

products.name: Dropps

certification.note: B Lab lists Dropps, PBC as a Certified B Corporation, and Dropps says it obtained Leaping Bunny certification in 2023.

ownership.note: The B Lab profile identifies Dropps as a PBC, but reviewed sources do not show co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: Dropps publishes a public timeline of B Corp, carbon-offset, Leaping Bunny and retail-access milestones.

environment.note: Dropps says its recyclable paperboard packaging has prevented more than 1 million plastic tubs and jugs from entering waste streams.

longevity.note: Dropps has current B Corp and cruelty-free signals, but the strongest public mission record is newer than long-running co-ops and legacy mission brands.

economical.note: Concentrated pods avoid heavy detergent jugs, but subscription/direct-to-consumer pricing can exceed basic supermarket detergent.

products.description: A B Corp laundry and dish detergent brand built around concentrated pods, cardboard packaging and cleaner-formulation claims.

products.name: Earth Breeze

certification.note: B Lab lists Earth Breeze, Inc. as a Certified B Corporation with a high overall B Impact Score.

ownership.note: Earth Breeze has strong B Corp certification, but reviewed sources do not show co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned control.

transparency.note: Earth Breeze publishes an impact page with donation-load totals and program framing for shelters and disaster relief.

environment.note: B Lab describes Earth Breeze as focused on replacing single-use plastic laundry packaging with waste-reducing detergent sheets.

longevity.note: Earth Breeze has current certification and impact claims, but its B Corp profile shows certification only since 2023.

economical.note: Detergent sheets are lighter and subscription-friendly, but per-load value still depends on cleaning performance and subscription pricing.

products.description: A high-scoring B Corp laundry-sheet brand with a large detergent-donation program and a plastic-jug replacement story.

products.name: Nature's Path Organic

certification.note: Nature's Path highlights certified organic, Non-GMO and Fair Trade product signals, but reviewed sources do not show current B Corp status.

ownership.note: Nature's Path says it was founded by Arran and Ratana Stephens and remains a family-run organic food company.

transparency.note: The company publishes history, family, organic, sustainability and community-impact pages rather than only product marketing.

environment.note: Nature's Path says all production facilities are zero waste and it is improving energy and water conservation.

longevity.note: Nature's Path history dates the company to 1985 and records decades of organic-food and sustainability milestones.

economical.note: Organic breakfast foods are widely available but usually cost more than commodity cereal and oatmeal.

products.description: A family-run organic breakfast-food company with a long organic track record and stronger ownership continuity than many acquired natural-food brands.

products.name: Brompton Bicycle

certification.note: Brompton says it received B Corp certification in July 2023, and B Lab lists Brompton Bicycle Limited as certified.

ownership.note: Brompton has current B Corp accountability, but reviewed sources do not show co-op, employee-owned or steward-owned governance.

transparency.note: Brompton publishes a sustainability page with B Corp score context, product-impact work and business challenges.

environment.note: Brompton frames its folding bikes as city mobility tools and reports product-longevity and repairability work through sustainability reporting.

longevity.note: B Lab says more than 1 million Brompton bikes have hit the roads since the first bike was made in 1975.

economical.note: Brompton bikes are durable transport tools but high upfront prices make them much less accessible than basic used bikes.

products.description: A B Corp folding-bike maker with a strong durability and urban-mobility case, offset by premium pricing and non-cooperative ownership.

products.name: Oatly

certification.note: Oatly publishes sustainability plans and reports, but reviewed current sources did not show B Corp or comparable mission-lock certification.

ownership.note: Oatly investor relations says Oatly ADSs trade on Nasdaq under ticker OTLY, making ownership less mission-locked than co-ops or trusts.

transparency.note: Oatly publishes investor filings, sustainability updates and product climate-footprint material.

environment.note: Oatly says its oat drinks have substantially lower climate impact than comparable cow's milk in multiple studies.

longevity.note: Oatly has a long plant-based brand history and public reporting, but the listed-company model adds market-pressure risk.

economical.note: Oatly is widely available in grocery and cafe channels, but branded oat milk often costs more than dairy or store-brand plant milk.

products.description: A mainstream plant-based milk brand with useful sustainability reporting and access, but public-company ownership keeps its mission lock limited.

products.name: Belu

certification.note: Belu explicitly says it is not a B Corp or carbon-neutral brand, choosing a social-enterprise and net-zero pathway instead.

ownership.note: Belu says it embeds purpose into ownership and governance and gives 100% of net profits to WaterAid.

transparency.note: Belu publishes profit-giving milestones and explains why it avoids some common certification/offset claims.

environment.note: Belu's own 2026 note favors a long-term net-zero pathway over carbon-neutral claims, which is transparent but less simple than a current certification badge.

longevity.note: WaterAid says its exclusive partnership with Belu began in 2011 and routes 100% of net profits into WaterAid's work.

economical.note: Belu's bottled water, filtration and hospitality products are mission-led but not generally the cheapest hydration route.

products.description: A UK social-enterprise drinks and filtration company that routes all net profits to WaterAid while avoiding over-simple carbon-neutral/B Corp claims.

products.name: Oboz Footwear

certification.note: Oboz says it is B Corp certified and uses the certification to guide social and environmental standards.

ownership.note: Oboz has B Corp accountability, but reviewed sources do not show co-op, steward-owned or employee-owned governance.

transparency.note: Oboz publishes B Corp and commitment pages, though public impact reporting is lighter than top-tier mission brands.

environment.note: Oboz frames its commitment around communities, climate and circularity, including tree planting and packaging changes.

longevity.note: Oboz's impact hub says the brand began in 2007 and has built its sustainability story around planting a tree for every pair sold.

economical.note: Outdoor footwear is a durable category, but Oboz hiking shoes are a premium purchase compared with basic everyday shoes.

products.description: A B Corp outdoor-footwear brand with tree-planting and sustainability commitments, useful for hiking buyers but not a low-cost shoe default.

products.name: Method

certification.note: Method product pages show cruelty-free and recycled-material claims, but reviewed current sources did not show a mission-lock or current B Corp profile.

ownership.note: SC Johnson says it acquired the Method and Ecover brands of People Against Dirty in 2018.

transparency.note: Method publishes product-level ingredient and packaging claims, but broader mission transparency is tied to the SC Johnson brand house.

environment.note: SC Johnson says reuse models across brands including Method and Ecover are part of its plastic-waste work.

longevity.note: Method remains a recognizable lower-impact cleaning brand under SC Johnson's lifestyle-brand portfolio, but acquisition weakened mission independence.

economical.note: Method is widely available and often less expensive than niche zero-waste brands, even though it is not the cheapest cleaning option.

products.description: A mainstream lower-impact cleaning brand whose accessibility is real, but whose mission-lock is limited after acquisition by SC Johnson.
